title: A generic constant sheaf on a normal Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $V$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], normal and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] in the sense of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], with generic point $\eta$, function field $K=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and generic inclusion $e:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$. For a finite abelian group $M$, let $\underline M_V$ and $\underline M_K$ be the constant sheaves on the etale sites [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then the natural map of etale sheaves $\underline M_V\to e_*\underline M_K$ is an isomorphism, where $e_*$ is the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: Apply the existing normal-scheme constant-unit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic] with coefficient ring ULift Z and module structure on the additive group M. The normality hypothesis supplies integrally closed stalks. This proves invertibility of the module adjunction unit for the inclusion of Spec of the generic stalk.

Let U be the functor forgetting modules to abelian groups, J the constant module sheaf, t the underlying module unit, and c its abelian adjoint. The canonical comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-inverse-image-comparison] makes c invertible. The adjunction equation is eta_Ab followed by f_*(c) = t. Since t and f_*(c) are invertible, eta_Ab is invertible on U(J). Mathlib constantCommuteCompose identifies U(J) with the constant abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; naturality of eta_Ab transports its invertibility to this sheaf.

The generic stalk is the function field [def-sc-function-field], a field for an integral scheme (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.FunctionField). Its residue map [def-weil-residue-field] is injective as a ring homomorphism from a field and surjective as a quotient map, hence invertible. Thus Spec of this map is an isomorphism. The residue-field inclusion is definitionally the composite of this isomorphism with the generic-stalk inclusion. Apply the unit-compatible composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]: the unit for the composite, followed by the pushforward of the pullback composition isomorphism, equals the composite-adjunction unit followed by the pushforward composition isomorphism. The unit along the scheme isomorphism is invertible because its pullback is an equivalence (Etale.isEquivalence_upperStar_of_isIso, constructed from identity and composition comparisons). Both factors of the composite-adjunction unit are invertible, so cancellation gives invertibility of the residue-field inclusion unit.

The displayed natural map is this invertible unit followed by the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of the canonical pullback-constant-sheaf identification [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A functor preserves isomorphisms, and a composite of isomorphisms is an isomorphism.
